claim: Neurodegenerative diseases are age-related disorders characterized by the cerebral accumulation of amyloidogenic proteins.
source: Neurodegenerative diseases are age-related disorders characterized by the cerebral accumulation of amyloidogenic proteins, and cellular senescence underlies their pathogenesis.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific understanding about neurodegenerative diseases, drawing from general scientific knowledge.

claim: Cellular senescence underlies the pathogenesis of neurodegenerative diseases.
source: Neurodegenerative diseases are age-related disorders characterized by the cerebral accumulation of amyloidogenic proteins, and cellular senescence underlies their pathogenesis.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations in the introduction section and represents current scientific understanding.

claim: Oral administration of ZSS hot water extract ameliorated Aβ and tau pathology in mouse models of Alzheimer's disease and frontotemporal dementia.
source: Oral administration of ZSS hot water extract ameliorated Aβ and tau pathology and cognitive impairment in mouse models of Alzheimer's disease and frontotemporal dementia.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in Figures 1 and 2 showing reduced pathology markers.

claim: Oral administration of ZSS hot water extract ameliorated cognitive impairment in mouse models of Alzheimer's disease and frontotemporal dementia.
source: Oral administration of ZSS hot water extract ameliorated Aβ and tau pathology and cognitive impairment in mouse models of Alzheimer's disease and frontotemporal dementia.
evidence: This is supported by behavioral test data shown in Figures 1A, 1B, and 2A.

claim: Non-extracted ZSS simple crush powder showed stronger effects than the extract in improving pathology and cognitive function.
source: Non-extracted ZSS simple crush powder showed stronger effects than the extract and improved α-synuclein pathology and cognitive/motor function in Parkinson's disease model mice.
evidence: This is supported by comparative experimental data in Figure 3 showing superior effects of powder versus extract.

claim: Non-extracted ZSS simple crush powder improved α-synuclein pathology in Parkinson's disease model mice.
source: Non-extracted ZSS simple crush powder showed stronger effects than the extract and improved α-synuclein pathology and cognitive/motor function in Parkinson's disease model mice.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data in Figure 4B showing reduced α-synuclein pathology markers.

claim: Non-extracted ZSS simple crush powder improved cognitive and motor function in Parkinson's disease model mice.
source: Non-extracted ZSS simple crush powder showed stronger effects than the extract and improved α-synuclein pathology and cognitive/motor function in Parkinson's disease model mice.
evidence: This is supported by behavioral test data in Figures 4A and 4E.

claim: ZSS powder suppressed cellular senescence in normal aged mice.
source: Furthermore, when administered to normal aged mice, the ZSS powder suppressed cellular senescence, reduced DNA oxidation, promoted brain-derived neurotrophic factor expression and neurogenesis, and enhanced cognition to levels similar to those in young mice.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data in Figure 5E showing reduced senescence markers.

claim: ZSS powder reduced DNA oxidation in normal aged mice.
source: Furthermore, when administered to normal aged mice, the ZSS powder suppressed cellular senescence, reduced DNA oxidation, promoted brain-derived neurotrophic factor expression and neurogenesis, and enhanced cognition to levels similar to those in young mice.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data in Figure 6A showing reduced 8-OHdG levels.

claim: ZSS powder promoted brain-derived neurotrophic factor expression in normal aged mice.
source: Furthermore, when administered to normal aged mice, the ZSS powder suppressed cellular senescence, reduced DNA oxidation, promoted brain-derived neurotrophic factor expression and neurogenesis, and enhanced cognition to levels similar to those in young mice.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data in Figure 5C showing increased BDNF expression.

claim: ZSS powder promoted neurogenesis in normal aged mice.
source: Furthermore, when administered to normal aged mice, the ZSS powder suppressed cellular senescence, reduced DNA oxidation, promoted brain-derived neurotrophic factor expression and neurogenesis, and enhanced cognition to levels similar to those in young mice.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data in Figure 5D showing increased neurogenesis.

claim: ZSS powder enhanced cognition in normal aged mice to levels similar to those in young mice.
source: Furthermore, when administered to normal aged mice, the ZSS powder suppressed cellular senescence, reduced DNA oxidation, promoted brain-derived neurotrophic factor expression and neurogenesis, and enhanced cognition to levels similar to those in young mice.
evidence: This is supported by behavioral test data in Figure 5A.

claim: The quantity of jujuboside A, jujuboside B, and spinosin was not proportional to the nootropic activity of ZSS.
source: The quantity of known active ingredients of ZSS, jujuboside A, jujuboside B, and spinosin was not proportional to the nootropic activity of ZSS.
evidence: This is supported by component analysis data in Table 1 and behavioral test data in Figure 7.

claim: ZSS simple crush powder is a promising dietary material for the prevention of neurodegenerative diseases and brain aging.
source: These results suggest that ZSS simple crush powder is a promising dietary material for the prevention of neurodegenerative diseases and brain aging.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: Aβ and tau accumulate in Alzheimer's disease.
source: Cerebral accumulation of amyloidogenic proteins is a hallmark of neurodegenerative diseases; Aβ and tau accumulate in Alzheimer's disease (AD), tau accumulates in frontotemporal dementia (FTD), and α-synuclein accumulates in Parkinson's disease (PD) and dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about AD pathology.

claim: Tau accumulates in frontotemporal dementia.
source: Cerebral accumulation of amyloidogenic proteins is a hallmark of neurodegenerative diseases; Aβ and tau accumulate in Alzheimer's disease (AD), tau accumulates in frontotemporal dementia (FTD), and α-synuclein accumulates in Parkinson's disease (PD) and dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about FTD pathology.

claim: α-synuclein accumulates in Parkinson's disease and dementia with Lewy bodies.
source: Cerebral accumulation of amyloidogenic proteins is a hallmark of neurodegenerative diseases; Aβ and tau accumulate in Alzheimer's disease (AD), tau accumulates in frontotemporal dementia (FTD), and α-synuclein accumulates in Parkinson's disease (PD) and dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about PD and DLB pathology.

claim: Amyloidogenic proteins aggregate into toxic oligomers and fibrils to induce synaptic dysfunction in patients' brains.
source: In patients' brains, these proteins aggregate into toxic oligomers and fibrils to induce synaptic dysfunction (Li and Selkoe, 2020; Gutierrez and Limon, 2022) and intercellular propagation of neuropathology (Jaunmuktane and Brandner, 2020; Umeda et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published research.

claim: Amyloidogenic proteins cause intercellular propagation of neuropathology.
source: In patients' brains, these proteins aggregate into toxic oligomers and fibrils to induce synaptic dysfunction (Li and Selkoe, 2020; Gutierrez and Limon, 2022) and intercellular propagation of neuropathology (Jaunmuktane and Brandner, 2020; Umeda et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published research.

claim: Cognitive function declines in AD, FTD, and DLB.
source: In consequence, cognitive function declines in AD, FTD, and DLB, and motor function is impaired in PD.
evidence: This is established clinical knowledge about these diseases.

claim: Motor function is impaired in PD.
source: In consequence, cognitive function declines in AD, FTD, and DLB, and motor function is impaired in PD.
evidence: This is established clinical knowledge about PD.

claim: The accumulation of amyloidogenic proteins begins decades before disease onset.
source: The accumulation of these proteins begins decades before the disease onset and many neurons die by the time clinical symptoms emerge (Jack et al., 2013; Ossenkoppele et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published research.

claim: Many neurons die by the time clinical symptoms emerge in neurodegenerative diseases.
source: The accumulation of these proteins begins decades before the disease onset and many neurons die by the time clinical symptoms emerge (Jack et al., 2013; Ossenkoppele et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published research.

claim: Early diagnosis and prevention are important for neurodegenerative diseases.
source: These findings indicate the importance of early diagnosis and prevention and that prophylactic agents for neurodegenerative diseases should have activities to remove toxic oligomers and repair damaged neurons.
evidence: This is inferred from the cited findings about disease progression.

claim: Prophylactic agents for neurodegenerative diseases should have activities to remove toxic oligomers and repair damaged neurons.
source: These findings indicate the importance of early diagnosis and prevention and that prophylactic agents for neurodegenerative diseases should have activities to remove toxic oligomers and repair damaged neurons.
evidence: This is a logical inference from the pathological mechanisms described.

claim: Neurodegenerative diseases are age-related disorders.
source: Neurodegenerative diseases are age-related disorders (Wyss-Coray, 2016; Hou et al., 2019), and recent evidence suggests that cellular senescence underlies their pathogenesis (Sahu et al., 2022; Shafqat et al., 2023).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published research.

claim: Recent evidence suggests that cellular senescence underlies the pathogenesis of neurodegenerative diseases.
source: Neurodegenerative diseases are age-related disorders (Wyss-Coray, 2016; Hou et al., 2019), and recent evidence suggests that cellular senescence underlies their pathogenesis (Sahu et al., 2022; Shafqat et al., 2023).
evidence: This is supported by citations to recent published research.

claim: Cellular senescence is a physiological phenomenon observed in aging in which proliferating cells undergo stable cell cycle arrest.
source: Cellular senescence is a physiological phenomenon observed in aging in which proliferating cells undergo stable cell cycle arrest.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about cellular senescence.

claim: Cellular senescence is induced by telomere attrition, epigenetic alterations, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, mechanical or shear stress, pathogens, and activation of oncogenes.
source: This phenomenon is induced by telomere attrition, epigenetic alterations, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, mechanical or shear stress, pathogens, and activation of oncogenes (Shafqat et al., 2023).
evidence: This is supported by citation to published research.

claim: In neurodegenerative diseases, abnormal protein accumulation triggers reactive oxygen species generation which causes oxidative stress and organelle dysfunction leading to cellular senescence.
source: In neurodegenerative diseases, abnormal protein accumulation triggers reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation which causes oxidative stress and organelle dysfunction leading to cellular senescence (Sahu et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citation to published research.

claim: Senescent cells accelerate the aging and damage of surrounding tissues through senescence-associated secretory phenotype.
source: Senescent cells accelerate the aging and damage of surrounding tissues through senescence-associated secretory phenotype composed of cytokines, chemokines, and growth factors (Sahu et al., 2022; Shafqat et al., 2023; González-Gualda et al., 2021), which in turn exacerbates neurodegenerating process.
evidence: This is supported by citations to published research.

claim: Senescence-associated secretory phenotype is composed of cytokines, chemokines, and growth factors.
source: Senescent cells accelerate the aging and damage of surrounding tissues through senescence-associated secretory phenotype composed of cytokines, chemokines, and growth factors (Sahu et al., 2022; Shafqat et al., 2023; González-Gualda et al., 2021), which in turn exacerbates neurodegenerating process.
evidence: This is supported by citations to published research.

claim: Senescence-associated secretory phenotype exacerbates neurodegenerating process.
source: Senescent cells accelerate the aging and damage of surrounding tissues through senescence-associated secretory phenotype composed of cytokines, chemokines, and growth factors (Sahu et al., 2022; Shafqat et al., 2023; González-Gualda et al., 2021), which in turn exacerbates neurodegenerating process.
evidence: This is supported by citations to published research.

claim: Eliminating senescent cells with dasatinib+quercetin ameliorated neuropathology, inflammation, and cognitive function in AD model mice.
source: Eliminating senescent cells with senolytic drugs, such as dasatinib+quercetin (D+Q), has been shown to ameliorate neuropathology, inflammation, and cognitive function in AD model mice (Zhang et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citation to published research.

claim: Cellular senescence is a target to prevent neurodegenerative diseases.
source: Thus, cellular senescence is another target to prevent neurodegenerative diseases.
evidence: This is inferred from the evidence about senescent cells' role in neurodegeneration.

claim: Two Aβ antibodies have been approved for neurodegenerative diseases.
source: Two Aβ antibodies have been approved, and tau and α-synuclein antibodies along with other Aβ antibodies are also in clinical trials.
evidence: This is factual information about current drug approvals.

claim: Tau and α-synuclein antibodies along with other Aβ antibodies are in clinical trials.
source: Two Aβ antibodies have been approved, and tau and α-synuclein antibodies along with other Aβ antibodies are also in clinical trials.
evidence: This is factual information about current clinical trials.

claim: Immunotherapy drugs for neurodegenerative diseases have problems in terms of cost, safety, and invasiveness.
source: However, these drugs have problems in terms of cost, safety, and invasiveness.
evidence: This is general knowledge about limitations of immunotherapy.

claim: Immunotherapy drugs for neurodegenerative diseases are generally very expensive.
source: They are generally very expensive, and their side effects are often serious.
evidence: This is general knowledge about immunotherapy costs.

claim: Side effects of immunotherapy drugs for neurodegenerative diseases are often serious.
source: They are generally very expensive, and their side effects are often serious.
evidence: This is general knowledge about immunotherapy safety.

claim: Patients must receive intravenous treatment at a hospital for immunotherapy drugs, which is a burden to the patient.
source: In addition, patients must receive intravenous treatment at a hospital, which is a burden to the patient.
evidence: This is general knowledge about immunotherapy administration.

claim: Immunotherapy treatments are not suitable for long-term prevention.
source: Such treatments are not suitable for long-term prevention.
evidence: This is inferred from the described limitations of immunotherapy.

claim: Prophylactic agents must be safe, inexpensive, and noninvasively available.
source: Prophylactic agents must be safe, inexpensive, and noninvasively available so that all asymptomatic and undiagnosed people can take them for a long period at their own discretion.
evidence: This is a logical requirement for preventive treatments.

claim: Prophylactic agents should be broadly effective against etiologic proteins, capable of repairing neurons, and effective at suppressing cellular senescence.
source: Also, they should be broadly effective against etiologic proteins, capable of repairing neurons, and effective at suppressing cellular senescence.
evidence: This is inferred from the pathological mechanisms of neurodegenerative diseases.

claim: These requirements are difficult to meet with single-ingredient pharmaceuticals.
source: These requirements are difficult to meet with single-ingredient pharmaceuticals, but it may be feasible by taking proper diets composed of multiple ingredients.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about pharmaceutical development.

claim: It may be feasible to meet prophylactic requirements by taking proper diets composed of multiple ingredients.
source: These requirements are difficult to meet with single-ingredient pharmaceuticals, but it may be feasible by taking proper diets composed of multiple ingredients.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about dietary approaches.

claim: Several herbs such as Rehmanniae radix, Polygalae radix, zizyphi spinosi semen, and Acorus tatarinowii/gramineus rhizome are claimed to be effective for amnesia in traditional Chinese medicine.
source: In search of materials for such diets, we explored medicinal herbs used in traditional Chinese medicine, where several herbs such as Rehmanniae radix (Jia et al., 2023), Polygalae radix (Zhao et al., 2020), zizyphi spinosi semen (ZSS) (Zhang et al., 2022), and Acorus tatarinowii/gramineus rhizome (Kim et al., 2022) are claimed to be effective for amnesia.
evidence: This is supported by citations to published research.

claim: ZSS is treated as a non-pharmaceutical in Japan.
source: In the present study, we focused on ZSS, the seeds of Ziziphus jujuba Miller var. spinosa, because ZSS is treated as a non-pharmaceutical in Japan but the other herbs are regarded as pharmaceuticals, i.e., not suitable for diets.
evidence: This is factual information about regulatory status in Japan.

claim: Rehmanniae radix, Polygalae radix, and Acorus tatarinowii/gramineus rhizome are regarded as pharmaceuticals in Japan.
source: In the present study, we focused on ZSS, the seeds of Ziziphus jujuba Miller var. spinosa, because ZSS is treated as a non-pharmaceutical in Japan but the other herbs are regarded as pharmaceuticals, i.e., not suitable for diets.
evidence: This is factual information about regulatory status in Japan.

claim: In traditional Chinese medicine, medicinal herbs are often subjected to decoction.
source: In traditional Chinese medicine, medicinal herbs are often subjected to decoction; the resultant extracts are taken as medicines but the extraction residues are usually discarded.
evidence: This is general knowledge about traditional Chinese medicine practices.

claim: The extraction residues of medicinal herbs also have some functional ingredients.
source: However, our previous studies revealed that the residues also have some functional ingredients and that hot water extraction tends to lose some volatile substances by evaporation and possibly break down some heat-sensitive components, which led us to conclude that simple crushing without extraction is a better way to maximize the effects of medicinal herbs (Umeda et al., 2024b; Umeda et al., 2024a).
evidence: This is supported by citations to the authors' previous studies.

claim: Hot water extraction tends to lose some volatile substances by evaporation and possibly break down some heat-sensitive components.
source: However, our previous studies revealed that the residues also have some functional ingredients and that hot water extraction tends to lose some volatile substances by evaporation and possibly break down some heat-sensitive components, which led us to conclude that simple crushing without extraction is a better way to maximize the effects of medicinal herbs (Umeda et al., 2024b; Umeda et al., 2024a).
evidence: This is supported by citations to the authors' previous studies.

claim: Simple crushing without extraction is a better way to maximize the effects of medicinal herbs.
source: However, our previous studies revealed that the residues also have some functional ingredients and that hot water extraction tends to lose some volatile substances by evaporation and possibly break down some heat-sensitive components, which led us to conclude that simple crushing without extraction is a better way to maximize the effects of medicinal herbs (Umeda et al., 2024b; Umeda et al., 2024a).
evidence: This is a conclusion inferred from the authors' previous studies.

claim: APP23 mice express human APP with the Swedish (KM670/671NL) mutation.
source: APP23 mice express human APP with the Swedish (KM670/671NL) mutation (Sturchler-Pierrat et al., 1997) and show Aβ oligomer accumulation, synapse loss, memory impairment, and amyloid deposition by 15 months (Umeda et al., 2021b).
evidence: This is supported by citation to published research.

claim: APP23 mice show Aβ oligomer accumulation, synapse loss, memory impairment, and amyloid deposition by 15 months.
source: APP23 mice express human APP with the Swedish (KM670/671NL) mutation (Sturchler-Pierrat et al., 1997) and show Aβ oligomer accumulation, synapse loss, memory impairment, and amyloid deposition by 15 months (Umeda et al., 2021b).
evidence: This is supported by citation to published research.

claim: ZSS extract at 0.1 mg/shot improved mouse memory in APP23 mice, but the effect was not complete.
source: The treatment improved mouse memory, but the effect was not complete (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral test data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: ZSS extract at 0.1 mg/shot significantly reduced the levels of Aβ oligomers in the cerebral cortex and hippocampus of APP23 mice.
source: ZSS extract significantly reduced the levels of Aβ oligomers (Figure 1C) and amyloid deposits (Figure 1D) in the cerebral cortex and hippocampus.
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: ZSS extract at 0.1 mg/shot significantly reduced amyloid deposits in the cerebral cortex and hippocampus of APP23 mice.
source: ZSS extract significantly reduced the levels of Aβ oligomers (Figure 1C) and amyloid deposits (Figure 1D) in the cerebral cortex and hippocampus.
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: ZSS extract at 0.1 mg/shot significantly recovered synaptophysin levels in the mossy fibers of hippocampal CA2/3 regions in APP23 mice.
source: Synaptophysin levels in the mossy fibers of hippocampal CA2/3 regions were significantly recovered by the treatment (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Tau784 mice express both 3-repeat and 4-repeat human tau with the dominant expression of 4-repeat human tau at adult age.
source: Tau784 mice express both 3-repeat and 4-repeat human tau with the dominant expression of 4-repeat human tau at adult age by the presence of a tau intron mutation (Umeda et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to published research.

claim: Tau784 mice exhibit tau hyperphosphorylation, tau oligomer accumulation, synapse loss, and memory impairment at 6 months.
source: They exhibit tau hyperphosphorylation, tau oligomer accumulation, synapse loss, and memory impairment at 6 months (Umeda et al., 2013; Umeda et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published research.

claim: ZSS extract improved mouse memory in Tau784 mice in a dose-dependent manner.
source: Mouse memory was improved in a dose-dependent manner; the higher dose achieved a complete recovery, reaching a level similar to that of non-Tg littermates, whereas the lower dose showed only a moderate effect (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral test data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: ZSS extract at 0.5 mg/shot achieved a complete recovery of memory in Tau784 mice, reaching a level similar to that of non-Tg littermates.
source: Mouse memory was improved in a dose-dependent manner; the higher dose achieved a complete recovery, reaching a level similar to that of non-Tg littermates, whereas the lower dose showed only a moderate effect (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral test data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: ZSS extract at 0.1 mg/shot showed only a moderate effect on memory in Tau784 mice.
source: Mouse memory was improved in a dose-dependent manner; the higher dose achieved a complete recovery, reaching a level similar to that of non-Tg littermates, whereas the lower dose showed only a moderate effect (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral test data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: ZSS extract significantly reduced the levels of phosphorylated tau in the hippocampus of Tau784 mice in a dose-dependent manner.
source: The levels of phosphorylated tau in the hippocampus and tau oligomers in the cerebral cortex were significantly reduced by the treatment in a dose-dependent manner (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: ZSS extract significantly reduced tau oligomers in the cerebral cortex of Tau784 mice in a dose-dependent manner.
source: The levels of phosphorylated tau in the hippocampus and tau oligomers in the cerebral cortex were significantly reduced by the treatment in a dose-dependent manner (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: ZSS extract significantly recovered synaptophysin levels in the hippocampal CA2/3 regions of Tau784 mice in a dose-dependent manner.
source: Synaptophysin levels in the hippocampal CA2/3 regions were also significantly recovered in a dose-dependent manner (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: ZSS simple crush powder markedly enhanced mouse memory in Tau784 mice to a level even higher than that of non-Tg littermates.
source: In contrast, the simple crush powder markedly enhanced mouse memory to a level even higher than that of non-Tg littermates.
evidence: This is supported by behavioral test data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: ZSS extraction residue showed only a moderate effect on memory in Tau784 mice, similar to that of the hot water extract.
source: On the other hand, the extraction residue showed only a moderate effect, similar to that of the hot water extract.
evidence: This is supported by behavioral test data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: All three ZSS preparations significantly attenuated the levels of phosphorylated tau in the hippocampus of Tau784 mice, with the simple crush powder showing the strongest effects.
source: The levels of phosphorylated tau in the hippocampus (Figure 3C) and tau oligomers in the cerebral cortex (Figure 3D) were significantly attenuated by all three preparations, with the simple crush powder showing the strongest effects.
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: All three ZSS preparations significantly attenuated tau oligomers in the cerebral cortex of Tau784 mice, with the simple crush powder showing the strongest effects.
source: The levels of phosphorylated tau in the hippocampus (Figure 3C) and tau oligomers in the cerebral cortex (Figure 3D) were significantly attenuated by all three preparations, with the simple crush powder showing the strongest effects.
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: ZSS simple crush powder significantly increased synaptophysin levels in the hippocampal CA2/3 regions of Tau784 mice to a level higher than that in non-Tg littermates.
source: Synaptophysin levels in the hippocampal CA2/3 regions were significantly recovered by the simple crush powder to a level higher than that in non-Tg littermates, whereas the hot water extract and extraction residue showed only slight effects (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: ZSS hot water extract and extraction residue showed only slight effects on synaptophysin levels in Tau784 mice.
source: Synaptophysin levels in the hippocampal CA2/3 regions were significantly recovered by the simple crush powder to a level higher than that in non-Tg littermates, whereas the hot water extract and extraction residue showed only slight effects (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Brain-derived neurotrophic factor promotes the growth and regeneration of neurons.
source: To evaluate the ability of ZSS to repair damaged neurons, we examined the expression level of brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF), which promotes the growth and regeneration of neurons (Colucci-D'Amato et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to published research.

claim: ZSS simple crush powder significantly increased BDNF expression in the hippocampus of Tau784 mice to a level even higher than that in non-Tg littermates.
source: The simple crush powder significantly increased BDNF expression in the hippocampus to a level even higher than that in non-Tg littermates (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: ZSS hot water extract and extraction residue showed only slight effects on BDNF expression in Tau784 mice.
source: In contrast, the hot water extract and extraction residue showed only slight effects on BDNF.
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: Huα-Syn(A53T) mice express human α-synuclein with A53T mutation.
source: Huα-Syn(A53T) mice express human α-synuclein with A53T mutation (Lee et al., 2002) and exhibit α-synuclein phosphorylation, α-synuclein oligomer accumulation, synapse loss, and memory impairment at 6 months, and motor dysfunction at 9 months, indicating that they can be used as a model of DLB at 6–8 months and as a model of PD after 9 months (Umeda et al., 2021a).
evidence: This is supported by citation to published research.

claim: Huα-Syn(A53T) mice exhibit α-synuclein phosphorylation, α-synuclein oligomer accumulation, synapse loss, and memory impairment at 6 months.
source: Huα-Syn(A53T) mice express human α-synuclein with A53T mutation (Lee et al., 2002) and exhibit α-synuclein phosphorylation, α-synuclein oligomer accumulation, synapse loss, and memory impairment at 6 months, and motor dysfunction at 9 months, indicating that they can be used as a model of DLB at 6–8 months and as a model of PD after 9 months (Umeda et al., 2021a).
evidence: This is supported by citation to published research.

claim: Huα-Syn(A53T) mice exhibit motor dysfunction at 9 months.
source: Huα-Syn(A53T) mice express human α-synuclein with A53T mutation (Lee et al., 2002) and exhibit α-synuclein phosphorylation, α-synuclein oligomer accumulation, synapse loss, and memory impairment at 6 months, and motor dysfunction at 9 months, indicating that they can be used as a model of DLB at 6–8 months and as a model of PD after 9 months (Umeda et al., 2021a).
evidence: This is supported by citation to published research.

claim: Huα-Syn(A53T) mice can be used as a model of DLB at 6–8 months and as a model of PD after 9 months.
source: Huα-Syn(A53T) mice express human α-synuclein with A53T mutation (Lee et al., 2002) and exhibit α-synuclein phosphorylation, α-synuclein oligomer accumulation, synapse loss, and memory impairment at 6 months, and motor dysfunction at 9 months, indicating that they can be used as a model of DLB at 6–8 months and as a model of PD after 9 months (Umeda et al., 2021a).
evidence: This is supported by citation to published research.

claim: ZSS powder significantly improved motor function of Huα-Syn(A53T) mice to a level similar to that of non-Tg littermates.
source: The treatment significantly improved motor function of Tg mice to a level similar to that of non-Tg littermates (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is supported by rotarod test data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: ZSS powder significantly reduced the levels of phosphorylated α-synuclein in the hippocampus of Huα-Syn(A53T) mice.
source: The levels of phosphorylated α-synuclein and α-synuclein oligomers in the hippocampus were significantly reduced by the treatment (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: ZSS powder significantly reduced α-synuclein oligomers in the hippocampus of Huα-Syn(A53T) mice.
source: The levels of phosphorylated α-synuclein and α-synuclein oligomers in the hippocampus were significantly reduced by the treatment (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: ZSS powder significantly enhanced BDNF expression in the cerebral cortex and substantia nigra of Huα-Syn(A53T) mice.
source: ZSS powder significantly enhanced BDNF expression in both brain regions (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The substantia nigra is particularly vulnerable to α-synuclein-induced neurodegeneration, leading to motor dysfunction in PD.
source: BDNF expression was examined in the cerebral cortex and substantia nigra; the latter brain region is particularly vulnerable to α-synuclein-induced neurodegeneration, leading to the motor dysfunction in PD.
evidence: This is established knowledge about PD pathology.

claim: Neurogenesis plays an important role in learning and memory.
source: Neurogenesis plays an important role in learning and memory and is shown to decrease in chronic stress, aging, and neurodegenerative diseases (Horgusluoglu et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to published research.

claim: Neurogenesis decreases in chronic stress, aging, and neurodegenerative diseases.
source: Neurogenesis plays an important role in learning and memory and is shown to decrease in chronic stress, aging, and neurodegenerative diseases (Horgusluoglu et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to published research.

claim: Neurogenesis in Huα-Syn(A53T) mice showed a tendency to decrease in the dentate gyrus and substantia nigra.
source: Neurogenesis in Tg mice showed a tendency to decrease in both brain regions (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is supported by neurogenesis data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: ZSS powder significantly increased neurogenesis in the dentate gyrus and substantia nigra of Huα-Syn(A53T) mice to levels higher than those in non-Tg littermates.
source: ZSS powder significantly increased neurogenesis to levels higher than those in non-Tg littermates.
evidence: This is supported by neurogenesis data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: ZSS powder is effective at repairing damaged neurons.
source: These results suggest that ZSS simple crush powder is effective at repairing damaged neurons.
evidence: This is inferred from the BDNF and neurogenesis data.

claim: ZSS powder significantly improved memory in 6- to 7-month-old Huα-Syn(A53T) mice to a level similar to or slightly less than that of non-Tg littermates.
source: Mouse memory was significantly improved to a level similar to or slightly less than that of non-Tg littermates (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral test data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: ZSS simple crush powder is a promising dietary material for preventing neurodegenerative diseases.
source: Taken together, these results suggest that ZSS simple crush powder is a promising dietary material for preventing neurodegenerative diseases.
evidence: This is a conclusion inferred from all the experimental results.

claim: Tau784 mice treated with ZSS simple crush powder displayed higher cognitive function than age-matched non-Tg littermates.
source: The finding that Tau784 mice treated with ZSS simple crush powder displayed higher cognitive function than age-matched non-Tg littermates (Figure 3A and B) led us to speculate that the powder has not only disease-preventing effects but also brain-rejuvenating effects.
evidence: This is supported by behavioral test data shown in Figures 3A and 3B.

claim: ZSS powder has brain-rejuvenating effects.
source: The finding that Tau784 mice treated with ZSS simple crush powder displayed higher cognitive function than age-matched non-Tg littermates (Figure 3A and B) led us to speculate that the powder has not only disease-preventing effects but also brain-rejuvenating effects.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the observation of enhanced cognition beyond normal levels.

claim: Cognitive function of aged mice was significantly lower than that of young mice.
source: As shown in Figure 5A, cognitive function of aged mice was significantly lower than that of young mice.
evidence: This is supported by behavioral test data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: ZSS powder significantly enhanced aged mice's cognition to a level similar to that of water-treated young mice.
source: ZSS powder significantly enhanced aged mice's cognition to a level similar to that of water-treated young mice.
evidence: This is supported by behavioral test data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: An enhanced memory was observed in ZSS-treated young mice, but it was not significant.
source: An enhanced memory was also observed in ZSS-treated young mice, but it was not significant.
evidence: This is supported by behavioral test data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: ZSS powder significantly increased synaptophysin levels in the hippocampal CA2/3 regions of aged mice, reaching levels similar to those in water-treated young mice.
source: Synaptophysin levels in the hippocampal CA2/3 regions (Figure 5B), BDNF expression in the hippocampus (Figure 5C), and neurogenesis in the dentate gyrus (Figure 5D) were significantly increased in ZSS-treated aged mice, reaching levels similar to those in water-treated young mice.
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: ZSS powder significantly increased BDNF expression in the hippocampus of aged mice, reaching levels similar to those in water-treated young mice.
source: Synaptophysin levels in the hippocampal CA2/3 regions (Figure 5B), BDNF expression in the hippocampus (Figure 5C), and neurogenesis in the dentate gyrus (Figure 5D) were significantly increased in ZSS-treated aged mice, reaching levels similar to those in water-treated young mice.
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: ZSS powder significantly increased neurogenesis in the dentate gyrus of aged mice, reaching levels similar to those in water-treated young mice.
source: Synaptophysin levels in the hippocampal CA2/3 regions (Figure 5B), BDNF expression in the hippocampus (Figure 5C), and neurogenesis in the dentate gyrus (Figure 5D) were significantly increased in ZSS-treated aged mice, reaching levels similar to those in water-treated young mice.
evidence: This is supported by neurogenesis data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Increased levels of synaptophysin and BDNF were observed in ZSS-treated young mice, but the effects were not significant.
source: Increased levels of synaptophysin and BDNF were also observed in ZSS-treated young mice, but the effects were not significant.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figures 5B and 5C.

claim: Cellular senescence is one of the hallmarks of aging.
source: Cellular senescence is one of the hallmarks of aging (López-Otín et al., 2023) and has been suggested to underlie the pathogenesis of neurodegenerative diseases (Sahu et al., 2022; Shafqat et al., 2023).
evidence: This is supported by citation to published research.

claim: p16INK4a and p21CIP1/WAF1 represent cell cycle arrest.
source: We measured the levels of cellular senescence focusing on its intracellular markers, p16INK4a, p21CIP1/WAF1, and γH2AX; the former two represent cell cycle arrest and the last one reflects DNA damage (Sahu et al., 2022; González-Gualda et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published research.

claim: γH2AX reflects DNA damage.
source: We measured the levels of cellular senescence focusing on its intracellular markers, p16INK4a, p21CIP1/WAF1, and γH2AX; the former two represent cell cycle arrest and the last one reflects DNA damage (Sahu et al., 2022; González-Gualda et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published research.

claim: The levels of p16INK4a, p21CIP1/WAF1, and γH2AX in the cerebral cortex of aged mice were significantly higher than those in young mice.
source: The levels of these markers in the cerebral cortex of aged mice were significantly higher than those in young mice (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: ZSS powder significantly reduced the levels of p16INK4a, p21CIP1/WAF1, and γH2AX in aged mice to levels similar to or lower than those in water-treated young mice.
source: ZSS powder significantly reduced them to levels similar to or lower than those in water-treated young mice (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: Reduced cellular senescence was observed for p21 and γH2AX in ZSS-treated young mice, but the effects were not significant.
source: Reduced cellular senescence was also observed for p21 and γH2AX in ZSS-treated young mice, but the effects were not significant.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: Cellular senescence is induced by DNA damage triggered by various stressors.
source: Cellular senescence is induced by DNA damage triggered by various stressors, and oxidative stress is a major cause of DNA damage (Nousis et al., 2023).
evidence: This is supported by citation to published research.

claim: Oxidative stress is a major cause of DNA damage.
source: Cellular senescence is induced by DNA damage triggered by various stressors, and oxidative stress is a major cause of DNA damage (Nousis et al., 2023).
evidence: This is supported by citation to published research.

claim: 8-hydroxy-2'-deoxyguanosine is a marker of DNA oxidation.
source: To evaluate the antioxidant effect of ZSS powder, we measured the levels of 8-hydroxy-2'-deoxyguanosine (8-OHdG), a marker of DNA oxidation (Valavanidis et al., 2009), and its autoantibodies (Ahmad et al., 2024) in the brains of ZSS-treated mice.
evidence: This is supported by citation to published research.

claim: The levels of 8-OHdG and its autoantibodies were both increased in aged mice.
source: The levels of 8-OHdG and its autoantibodies were both increased in aged mice, where the increase in autoantibodies was more pronounced than that in 8-OHdG (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is supported by biochemical data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: The increase in 8-OHdG autoantibodies was more pronounced than that in 8-OHdG in aged mice.
source: The levels of 8-OHdG and its autoantibodies were both increased in aged mice, where the increase in autoantibodies was more pronounced than that in 8-OHdG (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is supported by biochemical data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: When DNA oxidation products are continuously produced with aging, autoimmune response is strongly induced to remove them, and as a result, the increase in 8-OHdG is suppressed.
source: This may be because when DNA oxidation products are continuously produced with aging, autoimmune response is strongly induced to remove them, and as a result, the increase in 8-OHdG is suppressed.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the observed data pattern.

claim: Persistent immune reaction may cause chronic inflammation leading to cellular senescence.
source: Such a persistent immune reaction may cause chronic inflammation leading to cellular senescence.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the consequences of immune response.

claim: ZSS powder significantly reduced the levels of 8-OHdG and its autoantibodies in aged mice to levels similar to or lower than those in water-treated young mice.
source: ZSS powder significantly reduced the levels of 8-OHdG and its autoantibodies to levels similar to or lower than those in water-treated young mice.
evidence: This is supported by biochemical data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: ZSS powder quenched superoxide only weakly.
source: ZSS powder quenched superoxide only weakly (Figure 6B); its activity was about 1/100 of that of Mamaki leaf powder, which is known to have strong antioxidant activity (Kartika et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by radical-scavenging assay data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: The radical-scavenging activity of ZSS powder was about 1/100 of that of Mamaki leaf powder.
source: ZSS powder quenched superoxide only weakly (Figure 6B); its activity was about 1/100 of that of Mamaki leaf powder, which is known to have strong antioxidant activity (Kartika et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by radical-scavenging assay data shown in Figure 6B and citation.

claim: Mamaki leaf powder has strong antioxidant activity.
source: ZSS powder quenched superoxide only weakly (Figure 6B); its activity was about 1/100 of that of Mamaki leaf powder, which is known to have strong antioxidant activity (Kartika et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citation to published research.

claim: ZSS powder suppresses cellular senescence, at least in part, through its antioxidant action.
source: These results suggest that ZSS powder suppresses cellular senescence, at least in part, through its antioxidant action, but this effect is unlikely due to the direct action of ZSS components on free radicals.
evidence: This is inferred from the combined data on cellular senescence and oxidative stress markers.

claim: The antioxidant effect of ZSS powder is unlikely due to the direct action of ZSS components on free radicals.
source: These results suggest that ZSS powder suppresses cellular senescence, at least in part, through its antioxidant action, but this effect is unlikely due to the direct action of ZSS components on free radicals.
evidence: This is inferred from the weak radical-scavenging activity shown in Figure 6B.

claim: The major ingredients of ZSS are jujuboside A, jujuboside B, and spinosin.
source: The major ingredients of ZSS are jujuboside A, jujuboside B, and spinosin (Liu et al., 2007; Zhang et al., 2014; Hua et al., 2022), all of which have been reported to possess neuroprotective effects (Zhang et al., 2018; Tabassum et al., 2019; Liu et al., 2014; Jin et al., 2023; Ko et al., 2015; Lee et al., 2016; Xu et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published research.

claim: Jujuboside A, jujuboside B, and spinosin have been reported to possess neuroprotective effects.
source: The major ingredients of ZSS are jujuboside A, jujuboside B, and spinosin (Liu et al., 2007; Zhang et al., 2014; Hua et al., 2022), all of which have been reported to possess neuroprotective effects (Zhang et al., 2018; Tabassum et al., 2019; Liu et al., 2014; Jin et al., 2023; Ko et al., 2015; Lee et al., 2016; Xu et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published research.

claim: The ZSS simple crush powder contained less jujuboside A, jujuboside B, and spinosin than the hot water extract.
source: Contrary to our expectation, the powder contained less of these substances than the extract (Table 1).
evidence: This is supported by component analysis data shown in Table 1.

claim: A mixture of jujuboside A, jujuboside B, and spinosin at doses corresponding to those in 0.5 mg ZSS extract showed a much weaker effect on mouse memory than 0.5 mg ZSS extract.
source: This treatment showed a much weaker effect on mouse memory (Figure 7) than that of 0.5 mg ZSS extract (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral test data shown in Figures 7 and 2A.

claim: ZSS contains other active substances besides jujuboside A, jujuboside B, and spinosin.
source: These results suggest that ZSS contains other active substances besides jujuboside A, jujuboside B, and spinosin, and a significant portion of them may be lost during hot water extraction.
evidence: This is inferred from the component analysis and behavioral test results.

claim: A significant portion of ZSS active substances may be lost during hot water extraction.
source: These results suggest that ZSS contains other active substances besides jujuboside A, jujuboside B, and spinosin, and a significant portion of them may be lost during hot water extraction.
evidence: This is inferred from the comparison of extract and powder efficacy.

claim: ZSS removed Aβ, tau, and α-synuclein oligomers in mouse models of neurodegenerative diseases.
source: In the present study, we demonstrated that ZSS, particularly its non-extracted simple crush powder, has remarkable medicinal effects on neurodegenerative diseases. It removed Aβ, tau, and α-synuclein oligomers, restored synaptophysin levels, enhanced BDNF expression and neurogenesis, and improved cognitive and motor function in mouse models of AD, FTD, DLB, and PD.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data throughout the Results section.

claim: ZSS restored synaptophysin levels in mouse models of neurodegenerative diseases.
source: In the present study, we demonstrated that ZSS, particularly its non-extracted simple crush powder, has remarkable medicinal effects on neurodegenerative diseases. It removed Aβ, tau, and α-synuclein oligomers, restored synaptophysin levels, enhanced BDNF expression and neurogenesis, and improved cognitive and motor function in mouse models of AD, FTD, DLB, and PD.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data throughout the Results section.

claim: ZSS enhanced BDNF expression and neurogenesis in mouse models of neurodegenerative diseases.
source: In the present study, we demonstrated that ZSS, particularly its non-extracted simple crush powder, has remarkable medicinal effects on neurodegenerative diseases. It removed Aβ, tau, and α-synuclein oligomers, restored synaptophysin levels, enhanced BDNF expression and neurogenesis, and improved cognitive and motor function in mouse models of AD, FTD, DLB, and PD.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data throughout the Results section.

claim: ZSS improved cognitive and motor function in mouse models of AD, FTD, DLB, and PD.
source: In the present study, we demonstrated that ZSS, particularly its non-extracted simple crush powder, has remarkable medicinal effects on neurodegenerative diseases. It removed Aβ, tau, and α-synuclein oligomers, restored synaptophysin levels, enhanced BDNF expression and neurogenesis, and improved cognitive and motor function in mouse models of AD, FTD, DLB, and PD.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data throughout the Results section.

claim: In normal aged mice, ZSS powder reduced DNA oxidation and cellular senescence.
source: Furthermore, in normal aged mice, ZSS powder reduced DNA oxidation and cellular senescence, increased synaptophysin, BDNF, and neurogenesis, and enhanced cognition to levels similar to those in young mice.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data in Figures 5 and 6.

claim: In normal aged mice, ZSS powder increased synaptophysin, BDNF, and neurogenesis to levels similar to those in young mice.
source: Furthermore, in normal aged mice, ZSS powder reduced DNA oxidation and cellular senescence, increased synaptophysin, BDNF, and neurogenesis, and enhanced cognition to levels similar to those in young mice.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data in Figure 5.

claim: In normal aged mice, ZSS powder enhanced cognition to levels similar to those in young mice.
source: Furthermore, in normal aged mice, ZSS powder reduced DNA oxidation and cellular senescence, increased synaptophysin, BDNF, and neurogenesis, and enhanced cognition to levels similar to those in young mice.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data in Figure 5A.

claim: Neurodegenerative disease-prophylactic agents should have activities to remove toxic oligomers of etiologic proteins, repair damaged neurons, and suppress cellular senescence.
source: We proposed that neurodegenerative disease-prophylactic agents should have activities to remove toxic oligomers of etiologic proteins, repair damaged neurons, and suppress cellular senescence.
evidence: This is a proposal based on the pathological mechanisms of neurodegenerative diseases.

claim: ZSS powder meets the requirements for neurodegenerative disease-prophylactic agents.
source: Our results show that the ZSS powder meets these requirements.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results.

claim: ZSS is safe.
source: Since ZSS is safe (i.e. treated as a non-pharmaceutical in Japan), cheaper than medicines, and orally available, the powder can meet these demands as well.
evidence: This is based on the regulatory status of ZSS in Japan.

claim: ZSS is cheaper than medicines.
source: Since ZSS is safe (i.e. treated as a non-pharmaceutical in Japan), cheaper than medicines, and orally available, the powder can meet these demands as well.
evidence: This is general knowledge about the cost of herbal materials versus pharmaceuticals.

claim: ZSS is orally available.
source: Since ZSS is safe (i.e. treated as a non-pharmaceutical in Japan), cheaper than medicines, and orally available, the powder can meet these demands as well.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the oral administration method used in the study.

claim: Traditional Chinese medicines are generally formulated as a combination of several herbs.
source: Traditional Chinese medicines are generally formulated as a combination of several herbs.
evidence: This is general knowledge about traditional Chinese medicine practices.

claim: Combining multiple herbs can increase efficacy, reduce side effects, and create new synergy actions.
source: This is because combining multiple herbs can increase efficacy, reduce side effects, and create new synergy actions.
evidence: This is general knowledge about the rationale for herbal combinations in traditional Chinese medicine.

claim: Traditional Chinese medicine aims to cure disease by balancing the body rather than targeting specific symptoms or molecules.
source: In addition, traditional Chinese medicine aims to cure disease by balancing the body rather than targeting specific symptoms or molecules, which could be efficiently achieved by combining various herbal medicines.
evidence: This is general knowledge about the philosophy of traditional Chinese medicine.

claim: Yokukansan is a Chinese medicine often prescribed to relieve the peripheral symptoms of dementia in Japan.
source: For example, in Japan, a Chinese medicine called Yokukansan (Ikarashi and Mizoguchi, 2016) is often prescribed to relieve the peripheral symptoms of dementia, and it is composed of seven kinds of herbs not including ZSS.
evidence: This is factual information about medical practice in Japan, supported by citation.

claim: Yokukansan is composed of seven kinds of herbs not including ZSS.
source: For example, in Japan, a Chinese medicine called Yokukansan (Ikarashi and Mizoguchi, 2016) is often prescribed to relieve the peripheral symptoms of dementia, and it is composed of seven kinds of herbs not including ZSS.
evidence: This is factual information about the composition of Yokukansan.

claim: ZSS is prescribed in combination with other herbs to stabilize the mind and cure palpitation, anxiety, and insomnia, and improve amnesia.
source: As for ZSS, it is prescribed in combination with other herbs to stabilize the mind and cure palpitation, anxiety, and insomnia, and improve amnesia (Zhang et al., 2022; Hua et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published research.

claim: ZSS ameliorates core symptoms of dementia by clearing toxic protein oligomers and repairing damaged neurons, without being combined with other herbs.
source: Our results show that ZSS ameliorates core symptoms of dementia by clearing toxic protein oligomers and repairing damaged neurons, without being combined with other herbs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results.

claim: ZSS is effective on insomnia, depression, and anxiety.
source: Since ZSS is also effective on insomnia, depression, and anxiety (Zhang et al., 2022; Hua et al., 2022), ZSS could potentially be used alone for both the core and peripheral symptoms of dementia.
evidence: This is supported by citations to published research.

claim: ZSS could potentially be used alone for both the core and peripheral symptoms of dementia.
source: Since ZSS is also effective on insomnia, depression, and anxiety (Zhang et al., 2022; Hua et al., 2022), ZSS could potentially be used alone for both the core and peripheral symptoms of dementia.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on the observed effects of ZSS.

claim: Among the three preparations of ZSS tested, the simple crush powder displayed the strongest effects.
source: Among the three preparations of ZSS we tested, the simple crush powder displayed the strongest effects, and the extraction residue showed the same efficacy as the hot water extract.
evidence: This is supported by comparative experimental data in Figure 3.

claim: The extraction residue showed the same efficacy as the hot water extract.
source: Among the three preparations of ZSS we tested, the simple crush powder displayed the strongest effects, and the extraction residue showed the same efficacy as the hot water extract.
evidence: This is supported by comparative experimental data in Figure 3.

claim: A similar tendency of simple crush powder being more effective than extract was observed with other herbs, Mamaki and Acorus tatarinowii/gramineus leaves.
source: We had observed a similar tendency with other herbs, Mamaki and Acorus tatarinowii/gramineus leaves (Umeda et al., 2024b; Umeda et al., 2024a).
evidence: This is supported by citations to the authors' previous studies.

claim: Hot water extraction cannot necessarily recover all active ingredients of medicinal herbs.
source: These results support our previous hypothesis that hot water extraction cannot necessarily recover all active ingredients of medicinal herbs, rather, some functional components will be lost during the process.
evidence: This is a hypothesis supported by the comparative efficacy data.

claim: Some functional components of medicinal herbs will be lost during hot water extraction.
source: These results support our previous hypothesis that hot water extraction cannot necessarily recover all active ingredients of medicinal herbs, rather, some functional components will be lost during the process.
evidence: This is a hypothesis supported by the comparative efficacy data.

claim: Oral administration of jujuboside A promotes Aβ clearance and improves cognition in APP/PS1 mice.
source: For example, oral administration of jujuboside A promotes Aβ clearance and improves cognition in APP/PS1 mice (Zhang et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to published research.

claim: Intracerebroventricular injection of jujuboside A prevents sleep loss-induced memory impairment in APP/PS1 mice.
source: Furthermore, its intracerebroventricular injection prevents sleep loss-induced memory impairment in APP/PS1 mice (Tabassum et al., 2019) and ameliorates cognitive impairment in Aβ42-injected mice by reducing the level of Aβ42 (Liu et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to published research.

claim: Intracerebroventricular injection of jujuboside A ameliorates cognitive impairment in Aβ42-injected mice by reducing the level of Aβ42.
source: Furthermore, its intracerebroventricular injection prevents sleep loss-induced memory impairment in APP/PS1 mice (Tabassum et al., 2019) and ameliorates cognitive impairment in Aβ42-injected mice by reducing the level of Aβ42 (Liu et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to published research.

claim: Intraperitoneal administration of jujuboside B suppresses febrile seizure in lipopolysaccharide-injected mice.
source: Jujuboside B, when administered intraperitoneally, suppresses febrile seizure in lipopolysaccharide-injected mice (Jin et al., 2023).
evidence: This is supported by citation to published research.

claim: Oral administration of spinosin improves the cognition of Aβ42 oligomer-injected mice.
source: Oral administration of spinosin improves the cognition of Aβ42 oligomer-injected mice (Ko et al., 2015) and in adult mice increasing neurogenesis as well as the levels of BDNF (Lee et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to published research.

claim: Oral administration of spinosin increases neurogenesis and BDNF levels in adult mice.
source: Oral administration of spinosin improves the cognition of Aβ42 oligomer-injected mice (Ko et al., 2015) and in adult mice increasing neurogenesis as well as the levels of BDNF (Lee et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to published research.

claim: Intracerebroventricular injection of spinosin attenuates cognitive impairment and restores the levels of BDNF in Aβ42-injected mice.
source: Furthermore, its intracerebroventricular injection attenuates cognitive impairment and restores the levels of BDNF in Aβ42-injected mice (Xu et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citation to published research.

claim: The content of jujuboside A, jujuboside B, and spinosin in the simple crush powder was lower than that in the hot water extract.
source: Despite that the effects of simple crush powder were stronger than that of hot water extract (Figure 3), the content of the three compounds in the powder was lower than that in the extract (Table 1).
evidence: This is supported by component analysis data in Table 1.

claim: A mixture of jujuboside A, jujuboside B, and spinosin failed to improve mouse memory at doses equivalent to their amounts in 0.5 mg ZSS extract.
source: In addition, while ZSS extract sufficiently improved mouse memory at 0.5 mg/shot (Figure 2A), a mixture of jujuboside A, jujuboside B, and spinosin failed to do so at doses equivalent to their amounts in 0.5 mg ZSS extract (Figure 7).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral test data in Figures 2A and 7.

claim: The active components of ZSS are other than jujuboside A, jujuboside B, or spinosin.
source: These results suggest that the active components of ZSS are other than jujuboside A, jujuboside B, or spinosin.
evidence: This is inferred from the component analysis and efficacy comparison data.

claim: The antioxidant activity of ZSS powder is not due to the direct action of ZSS components on free radicals.
source: In aged mice, ZSS powder reduced the levels of 8-OHdG and its autoantibodies in the brain (Figure 6A); nevertheless, the radical-scavenging ability of ZSS powder was very weak (Figure 6B), suggesting that the antioxidant activity of ZSS powder is not due to the direct action of ZSS components on free radicals.
evidence: This is inferred from the comparison of in vivo antioxidant effects and in vitro radical-scavenging activity.

claim: Plant-derived dietary fibers can make the intestinal environment favorable for gut microbes and consequently affect brain function.
source: It has been shown that plant-derived dietary fibers can make the intestinal environment favorable for gut microbes and consequently affect brain function (Puhlmann and de Vos, 2022; Cuervo-Zanatta et al., 2023).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published research.

claim: The effects of ZSS powder on neuropathology, cognitive and motor function, oxidative stress, and cellular senescence may be attributed, to a greater or lesser extent, to the action of dietary fibers on gut microbiota.
source: The effects of ZSS powder on neuropathology, cognitive and motor function, oxidative stress, and cellular senescence may be attributed, to a greater or lesser extent, to the action of dietary fibers on gut microbiota.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the mechanism of action.

claim: ZSS extraction residue is expected to contain a significant amount of dietary fibers.
source: ZSS extraction residue is also expected to contain a significant amount of dietary fibers, which may account for its nootropic activity.

claim: Dietary fibers in ZSS extraction residue may account for its nootropic activity.
source: ZSS extraction residue is also expected to contain a significant amount of dietary fibers, which may account for its nootropic activity.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the mechanism of action.

claim: ZSS has a broad spectrum against Aβ, tau, and α-synuclein.
source: The present study showed that ZSS has a broad spectrum against Aβ, tau, and α-synuclein, but it remains to be studied whether ZSS is also effective against TDP-43, another protein accumulated in FTD and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data throughout the Results section.

claim: It remains to be studied whether ZSS is also effective against TDP-43.
source: The present study showed that ZSS has a broad spectrum against Aβ, tau, and α-synuclein, but it remains to be studied whether ZSS is also effective against TDP-43, another protein accumulated in FTD and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of the current study.

claim: TDP-43 is a protein accumulated in FTD and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.
source: The present study showed that ZSS has a broad spectrum against Aβ, tau, and α-synuclein, but it remains to be studied whether ZSS is also effective against TDP-43, another protein accumulated in FTD and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.
evidence: This is established knowledge about TDP-43 pathology.

claim: The mouse models used do not fully represent human pathology.
source: Furthermore, we used three different mouse models of neurodegenerative diseases, but they do not fully represent human pathology, and, therefore, clinical studies are required to evaluate the true efficacy of ZSS in humans.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of animal models.

claim: Clinical studies are required to evaluate the true efficacy of ZSS in humans.
source: Furthermore, we used three different mouse models of neurodegenerative diseases, but they do not fully represent human pathology, and, therefore, clinical studies are required to evaluate the true efficacy of ZSS in humans.
evidence: This is a logical inference about the need for human studies.

claim: ZSS has a long history of traditional Chinese medicine.
source: ZSS has a long history of traditional Chinese medicine and can be treated as a non-pharmaceutical in Japan, suggesting its safety.
evidence: This is general knowledge about ZSS.

claim: The safety of the long-term intake of ZSS powder needs to be confirmed.
source: However, since simple crushing is a different processing method than usual, the safety of the long-term intake of ZSS powder needs to be confirmed.
evidence: This is a logical inference about the need for safety studies.

claim: ZSS powder has antiaging effects.
source: Our results suggest that ZSS powder has antiaging effects.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data in Figures 5 and 6.

claim: Twelve hallmarks of aging have been proposed, including cellular senescence, stem cell exhaustion, epigenetic alterations, loss of proteostasis, chronic inflammation, dysbiosis, and so on.
source: Twelve hallmarks of aging have been proposed, including cellular senescence, stem cell exhaustion, epigenetic alterations, loss of proteostasis, chronic inflammation, dysbiosis, and so on (López-Otín et al., 2023).
evidence: This is supported by citation to published research.

claim: Clarifying which hallmarks of aging are improved by ZSS powder would help understand its antiaging effects more clearly.
source: By clarifying which of these hallmarks, in addition to cellular senescence, are improved by ZSS powder, the antiaging effects of the powder can be more clearly understood.
evidence: This is a logical inference about future research directions.

claim: Identification of the true active components in ZSS powder may be necessary to develop ZSS-derived functional foods.
source: Although we don't know the true active components in ZSS powder, and their identification may be necessary to develop ZSS-derived functional foods, our findings suggest that ZSS simple crush powder is a promising dietary material for the prevention of neurodegenerative diseases and brain aging.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about future research needs.

claim: ZSS simple crush powder is a promising dietary material for the prevention of neurodegenerative diseases and brain aging.
source: Although we don't know the true active components in ZSS powder, and their identification may be necessary to develop ZSS-derived functional foods, our findings suggest that ZSS simple crush powder is a promising dietary material for the prevention of neurodegenerative diseases and brain aging.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from all the experimental results.
